case.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
case.head: 9df83c38409c8bfad0517aebffe48211eda4a5b4

requirements.text: The reported consuming-project build must complete cleanly rather than failing the generator with CS8785 and the analyzer with AD0001/IndexOutOfRangeException.
requirements.quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

requirements.text: The consuming app must receive a generated MessagePack resolver instead of silently having none.
The addressed scenario is a closed generic value type, including the repro's generic record struct, defined in a referenced assembly and used as a member type.
requirements.quote: So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**.

requirements.text: Avoiding metadata-syntax crashes should not unnecessarily discard diagnostics for source declarations in the compilation being analyzed.
requirements.quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

added: Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.
this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);
/// Gets the location of the identifier of a property, if it is declared in source.
/// <param name="property">The property symbol. It may be declared in metadata, in which case <see langword="null" /> is returned.</param>
/// <returns>The location of the identifier, or <see langword="null" /> if the property has no declaration in source.</returns>
/// Reports a diagnostic only when its location belongs to the compilation being analyzed.
/// Types and members that come from metadata (or from another compilation) have no location in the compilation being analyzed.
/// Their problems are reported by the compilation that defines them, so they are dropped here rather than being reported
/// against a location that does not exist, which analyzers are not permitted to do.
/// Asserts that a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly (metadata only, no syntax),

findings.statement: The documentation presents defining-project reporting as a guarantee, but the implementation only suppresses the diagnostic in the consuming compilation and the new helper emits the defining assembly without running analyzers on it. The documentation would be inaccurate for such a case even though consumer-side suppression itself is intentional.
